answer: A vesting-and-clawback defense makes sybil farming a bad bet: rewards an agent earns are not paid out at once but released gradually over later epochs, like an ember banked overnight that only stays lit if the fire is tended honestly. During the vesting window, peers audit the agent's work; if duplicate identities or copied outputs are found, the unvested balance is burned. A ferrous lock on quick exits means a farmer cannot grab rewards and vanish: each clone must survive weeks of scrutiny across the whole meadow of agents, paying upkeep while honest agents simply collect on schedule.
